prior_year_events.impact_description: Adverse development on older underwriting years resulting in a gross strengthening of reserves driven primarily by the 2021 underwriting year

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2023 gross claims outstanding were GBP 19.626m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows a net adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 5.947m (strengthening), driven primarily by the 2021 underwriting year, resulting in higher gross claims estimates for prior years.
raw_causal_phrases: large catastrophe claims where uncertainly is initially great.
The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.

The uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience of an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin for future experience potentially being more adverse than assumed is at its highest.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (cumulative gross claims incurred by underwriting year) found on page 36. The report does not provide a single explicit sentence stating the gross prior-year movement. Triangle values were presented in GBP '000 and converted to millions. The result excludes 2023 and 2022 (the two most recent underwriting years) per the standard method. No specific named events were identified in the document as driving the prior year movement.
